about: Before/after quiz for playtests (only with ?playtest=1). 'answer' is the index of the right option (0 = the first). The questions are general on purpose (not about one country's law), so anyone can take them, and every one is something the game shows: the wind decides which side of a village is in danger and can push a fire downhill; eucalyptus and pine burn more fiercely than broadleaf trees; less fuel means weaker flames; Portugal's law (Decreto-Lei 82/2021) asks for cleared strips around homes and along roads (the glowing tiles), and FireSmart Canada gives similar advice for the ground around homes. Options have similar lengths and the right answer is in a different place each time, so it cannot be guessed from its shape. The order matters: no question gives away the answer to a later one.

questions.question: A strong wind blows from the north (toward the south). Fires could start in the forest on any side of a village. On which side does a firebreak (a strip of bare ground that fire cannot cross) protect the houses best?
questions.explanation: Wind pushes a fire downwind. A fire on the north side is blown straight at the houses, so a firebreak on that side meets it first. Fires on the other sides are blown away from the village. In the game, the wind arrow shows where a fire will go.

questions.question: You only have money to clear dry bushes in a few places. Where does it protect a village the most?
options: Deep in the forest, where most of the trees are
On the hilltops, where a fire is easy to spot
In a strip right around the houses and along the roads
In the gardens and parks in the middle of the village
questions.explanation: A fire has to cross that strip to reach the houses, and roads are how people escape. In the game, these strips are the glowing tiles. Portugal's law asks for them, and FireSmart Canada gives the same advice for the ground around homes.

questions.question: Which kind of forest usually burns more fiercely?
questions.explanation: Eucalyptus leaves are full of oil and pine has sticky resin: both catch fire easily. Broadleaf trees like oak, birch and aspen have moister leaves and slow a fire down. That is why the game lets you replace eucalyptus with broadleaf trees.

questions.question: A strong wind blows down a hill toward a village. A fire starts on the hilltop. What happens?
options: It stays near the top, because fire only climbs uphill
The wind can push it down the hill to the village
It spreads at the same speed in every direction
questions.explanation: Fire climbs slopes fastest, but a strong wind can push it downhill too. On 6 October 2018 a north wind drove a fire down the Serra de Sintra toward Malveira da Serra: the night in the game.

questions.question: What does clearing dry bushes do when a wildfire arrives?
options: The wind slows down near the ground
The ground stays wet, so the fire goes out
There is less to burn, so the flames are smaller
questions.explanation: Dry bushes are fuel (in the game: "dry scrub", cleared with "Clear brush"). With less of them, the flames that arrive are weaker and flying embers have less to light.
